questions.stem: Which operation belongs in CLZ-370's pull-request workflow without Azure credentials?

options.A: Azure resource apply

optionExplanations.A: Apply needs authorization and changes Azure.
optionExplanations.B: These checks examine Terraform configuration without deploying.
optionExplanations.C: Key Vault retrieval is an authenticated data operation.
optionExplanations.D: Destroy is outside credential-free source checks.

questions.stem: What Azure resource does the manual OIDC example actually create as written?

options.A: The tagged resource group automatically
options.D: None; it stops at a plan

optionExplanations.A: A proposed change is not deployed by plan.
optionExplanations.B: The target contains only a resource-group proposal.
optionExplanations.C: Bastion is not in the target.
optionExplanations.D: The workflow contains no apply step.

questions.stem: What replaces a stored client secret in the manual example's authentication path?

options.A: A federated OIDC token exchange
options.D: A Key Vault secret printed into a plan

optionExplanations.A: Federation uses the configured identity trust.
optionExplanations.B: Committed credentials are explicitly avoided.
optionExplanations.C: Azure access still requires authentication.
optionExplanations.D: Printing a secret is unnecessary disclosure.

questions.stem: Why does the OIDC workflow request id-token: write?

options.A: To make GITHUB_TOKEN a subscription Owner
options.C: To request an OIDC token for federation

optionExplanations.A: Azure role assignments remain separate.
optionExplanations.B: No apply is added by this permission.
optionExplanations.C: It permits token issuance for the configured trust.
optionExplanations.D: The permission is not blanket secret publication.

questions.stem: Why is contents: read appropriate for these examples?

options.A: It grants Contributor on every Azure resource
options.C: Checkout needs repository reads while no source-write operation is required

optionExplanations.A: GitHub permissions do not assign Azure RBAC.
optionExplanations.B: Key Vault authorization is separate.
optionExplanations.C: Repository and cloud permissions are distinct.
optionExplanations.D: Reviewers need separate environment configuration.

questions.stem: What must an authorized owner configure for azure-lab-plan before enabling the authenticated example?

options.A: Environment approval policy and scoped federation settings

optionExplanations.A: The plan requires a deliberate cloud trust and approval boundary.
optionExplanations.B: Design colors do not grant cloud identity trust.
optionExplanations.C: Monitor resources do not define GitHub environment approval.
optionExplanations.D: A title does not configure security.

questions.stem: OIDC login fails. Which values should be compared with the federated credential?

options.A: Only the Terraform resource tags

optionExplanations.A: Tags do not establish the token trust.
optionExplanations.B: Retention is unrelated.
optionExplanations.C: No VMSS is planned here.
optionExplanations.D: Federation relies on matching token claims and trust configuration.

questions.stem: A credential trusts one branch subject but the workflow uses a protected environment. What is the likely issue?

options.A: Terraform cannot run on Windows
options.B: The expected OIDC subject may not match the environment-based token
options.C: The action group blocks all logins
options.D: The DNS TTL is too long

optionExplanations.A: These examples explicitly use Windows runners.
optionExplanations.B: The federated subject must match the actual workflow context.
optionExplanations.C: No action group is part of the login path.
optionExplanations.D: DNS TTL is not this claim mismatch.

questions.stem: Which trio supplies the cloud identity context in the manual workflow?

options.A: AZURE_CLIENT_ID, AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID

optionExplanations.A: Those variables identify the federated application, tenant, and subscription.
optionExplanations.B: These VM inputs are unrelated to login.
optionExplanations.C: Traffic-routing inputs are unrelated.
optionExplanations.D: Browser fields cannot authenticate to Azure.

questions.stem: Why use the exact subscription ID variable instead of relying on a display name?

options.A: Display names automatically encrypt state
options.B: The ID removes Azure role checks
options.C: It makes the intended cloud scope explicit

optionExplanations.A: Names do not encrypt state.
optionExplanations.B: RBAC still applies.
optionExplanations.C: An exact GUID avoids ambiguity about the target.
optionExplanations.D: Selecting an ID does not create a subscription.

questions.stem: The examples reference full action commit SHAs. What benefit is intended?

options.A: Guaranteed freedom from every future vulnerability

optionExplanations.A: Pinned code can still need security updates.
optionExplanations.B: SHA pinning stabilizes the code being executed.
optionExplanations.C: Action pins do not approve cloud mutations.
optionExplanations.D: Pins still require reviewed maintenance.

questions.stem: A new security fix is available for a pinned action. What should maintainers do?

options.A: Replace it with an unreviewed floating branch
options.C: Ignore it because pins never need changes
options.D: Review and update its full commit pin

optionExplanations.A: Floating code loses the reviewed version boundary.
optionExplanations.B: Permission expansion is unrelated.
optionExplanations.C: Pinning does not eliminate maintenance.
optionExplanations.D: Immutable pins need deliberate upgrades.

questions.stem: What starts the authenticated Azure plan example?

options.A: Every documentation page view
options.B: Every pull request from any fork automatically

optionExplanations.A: Site viewing cannot dispatch it.
optionExplanations.B: It is separate from credential-free PR validation.
optionExplanations.C: Formatting does not trigger authenticated cloud plans.
optionExplanations.D: The example is manually triggered behind its environment gate.

questions.stem: Why initialize with -backend=false for credential-free checks?

options.A: Disable all provider installation
options.B: Avoid configuring a cloud state backend for syntax validation

optionExplanations.A: Providers may still need installation for validation.
optionExplanations.B: It supports checks without remote backend access.
optionExplanations.C: The flag does not erase state.
optionExplanations.D: Initialization never becomes apply because of that flag.

questions.stem: What does -lockfile=readonly enforce during the example initialization?

options.A: Do not read any configuration file
options.C: Do not modify the dependency lock file

optionExplanations.A: Configuration is still read.
optionExplanations.B: This is not an Azure resource lock.
optionExplanations.C: It uses the recorded dependency selections without rewriting them.
optionExplanations.D: Dependency verification remains relevant.

questions.stem: A branch deliberately contains unformatted Terraform. What should the credential-free workflow demonstrate?

options.A: A failing fmt check without an Azure deployment

optionExplanations.A: The exercise isolates a source-quality failure.
optionExplanations.B: The validation workflow does not apply.
optionExplanations.C: No backend deletion is configured.
optionExplanations.D: Credentials are not required or emailed.

questions.stem: terraform validate succeeds. What has it not proven?

options.A: The configuration was checked for internal validity
options.B: A future Azure apply will satisfy permissions, quota, and live service conditions

optionExplanations.A: Configuration validation is its purpose.
optionExplanations.B: Static validation is not a live deployment guarantee.
optionExplanations.C: Parsing is part of validation.
optionExplanations.D: Static expression checks are part of validation.

questions.stem: Why copy the selected example into the repository root's .github/workflows as .yml?

options.A: That is the location used for enabled repository workflows
options.C: MkDocs runs every file under a lesson folder
options.D: Azure Portal imports all YAML on login

optionExplanations.A: The lesson's examples are inert until deliberately enabled there.
optionExplanations.B: The .example files are teaching material.
optionExplanations.C: Docs hosting does not execute lesson workflows.
optionExplanations.D: Azure login does not import repository YAML.

questions.stem: A copied workflow cannot find Terraform files. What should be checked?

options.A: The lesson's browser theme
options.D: Its working-directory relative to repository root

optionExplanations.A: Theme does not select runner paths.
optionExplanations.B: Storage replication is unrelated.
optionExplanations.C: Routing health does not locate configuration files.
optionExplanations.D: Copying the example changes its enabled location, so paths must still resolve.

questions.stem: The manual plan uses -refresh=false. What evidence limitation follows?

options.A: It guarantees all Azure APIs are never contacted
options.C: It does not refresh existing remote object state for this plan
options.D: It applies the proposed resource group

optionExplanations.A: Providers may still interact with APIs during planning.
optionExplanations.B: Authentication remains necessary.
optionExplanations.C: Skipping refresh can omit current external changes.
optionExplanations.D: The command is still plan-only.

questions.stem: Why define workflow concurrency for this plan example?

options.A: Avoid overlapping runs in the defined group
options.B: Grant a state lock across every repository
options.D: Guarantee no human can run Terraform locally

optionExplanations.A: Workflow concurrency coordinates runs, not all possible Terraform writers.
optionExplanations.B: It is not universal backend locking.
optionExplanations.C: Approval policy is separately configured.
optionExplanations.D: Local commands remain outside that workflow group.

questions.stem: What risk does a bounded job timeout reduce?

options.A: All Azure authorization errors
options.D: A stuck workflow consuming runner time indefinitely

optionExplanations.A: It does not grant permissions.
optionExplanations.B: It cannot replace review.
optionExplanations.C: DNS timing is outside runner lifetime controls.
optionExplanations.D: A timeout bounds how long the runner job can remain active.

questions.stem: OIDC login succeeds but the resource-group plan is forbidden. What needs review?

options.A: Only contents: write on GitHub
options.C: The application's required Azure role and intended scope

optionExplanations.A: Repository write permission does not assign cloud rights.
optionExplanations.B: CSS has no cloud authorization role.
optionExplanations.C: Successful identity authentication does not guarantee Azure authorization.
optionExplanations.D: Workflow syntax checking is separate.

questions.stem: A workflow is extended to save a binary plan. What handling should be assessed?

options.A: Automatic public download for every user
options.B: Restricted access and short retention because plans may contain secrets
options.D: Assuming sensitive output redaction removes all values

optionExplanations.A: Public publication can leak planned secret values.
optionExplanations.B: Plans require secret-aware artifact handling.
optionExplanations.C: Artwork is not protected plan storage.
optionExplanations.D: Redaction does not remove plan values.

questions.stem: Which inspection follows the lesson's workflow acceptance criteria?

options.A: Print all environment credentials
options.B: Run destroy in the root folder
options.C: Check examples contain no terraform apply or client-secret step
options.D: Rename all workflow variables to password

optionExplanations.A: Printing credentials defeats safe validation.
optionExplanations.B: Destroy is unrelated to workflow acceptance.
optionExplanations.C: The lesson explicitly checks plan-only and secret-free workflow structure.
optionExplanations.D: Misleading names do not verify security.

questions.stem: A team now needs deployment automation. What should be designed beyond this example?

options.A: Add apply to every fork PR immediately
options.B: A separately approved apply operation with reviewed plan and scoped identity
options.D: Treat a successful quiz as Azure approval

optionExplanations.A: Untrusted PRs should not automatically mutate cloud resources.
optionExplanations.B: The lesson intentionally provides no apply implementation.
optionExplanations.C: Removing the gate weakens the intended boundary.
optionExplanations.D: Learner progress is not deployment authorization.

questions.stem: What does cleanup remove after using only the validation example?

options.A: Test workflow copies and local plan artifacts, with no Azure resources to destroy

optionExplanations.A: The examples do not deploy Azure resources.
optionExplanations.B: Subscription-wide deletion is outside scope.
optionExplanations.C: The backend belongs to another lesson.
optionExplanations.D: Branches are not the documented cleanup target.

questions.stem: An owner created a test federated credential for this lesson. Does removing the local YAML automatically delete it?

options.A: Yes; every file deletion calls Azure
options.B: Yes; terraform fmt destroys identity trusts
options.D: No; remove that external test configuration separately when appropriate

optionExplanations.A: File deletion is not an Azure API operation.
optionExplanations.B: Formatting does not mutate identity trust.
optionExplanations.C: Browser state has no identity lifecycle role.
optionExplanations.D: Federated identity configuration is outside the workflow-copy lifecycle.

questions.stem: Which tool checks the syntax and expressions of the supplied workflow examples?

options.A: actionlint

optionExplanations.A: The lesson invokes actionlint on both example files.
optionExplanations.B: DNS lookup does not lint workflow YAML.
optionExplanations.C: Secret reads do not lint actions.
optionExplanations.D: TCP checks do not inspect workflow syntax.

questions.stem: A passing authenticated workflow ends after terraform plan. What is valid to report?

options.A: The resource group was deployed and validated
options.B: The plan ran; deployment remains unperformed

optionExplanations.A: No apply evidence exists.
optionExplanations.B: A plan reports proposed changes without applying them.
optionExplanations.C: This example does not deploy the capstone.
optionExplanations.D: Planning does not prove unrelated cost cleanup.
